title: A filtered colimit of algebras is the colimit of the underlying modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small filtered category and $i\mapsto A_i$ a functor from $I$ to the category of commutative $R$-algebras, with transition maps $A(u):A_i\to A_j$ for $u:i\to j$, colimit $A=\varinjlim_IA_i$ in that category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\iota_i:A_i\to A$. Regard every $A_i$ and $A$ as $R$-modules and the $R$-algebra homomorphisms $A(u)$, $\iota_i$ as $R$-linear maps. Then $(A,(\iota_i)_{i\in I})$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto A_i$ in the category of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for every $R$-module $P$ and $R$-linear maps $f_i:A_i\to P$ with $f_j\circ A(u)=f_i$ for all $u:i\to j$ there is exactly one $R$-linear map $f:A\to P$ with $f\circ\iota_i=f_i$ for all $i$.

source.place: not stated in Stacks for algebras; the module side is Algebra, Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778: elements of the colimit are classes of elements of the stages, sums and scalar multiples computed at a common later index), and the passage from the colimit of rings to the colimit of modules is used implicitly in Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07RI (lemma-colimit-etale, line 47654) and More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH1 (more-algebra-lemma-filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres); the directed-set case with base A_0 is written out in step 2 of lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise

proof.text: *Step 1 (elements of $A$ and when two are equal).* By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise], applied to $R$, the filtered category $I$ and the diagram $i\mapsto A_i$ with its colimit $(A,(\iota_i))$: (a) $(A,(\iota_i))$ is also a colimit of the underlying diagram $i\mapsto A_i$ of commutative rings (transition maps $A(u)$); (b) every $z\in A$ is $\iota_i(a)$ for some $i\in I$ and $a\in A_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero], applied to the small filtered category $I$ and the colimit (a) of commutative rings: (c) for $a\in A_i$, $b\in A_j$ one has $\iota_i(a)=\iota_j(b)$ if and only if there are an object $k$ and morphisms $u:i\to k$, $v:j\to k$ with $A(u)(a)=A(v)(b)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778) and its proof: elements of a filtered colimit are classes of elements of the stages, sums and scalar multiples computed at a common later index; transcribed here to the colimit of commutative R-algebras regarded as R-modules

proof.text: *Step 2 (a cocone of $R$-modules).* An $R$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:B\to B'$ of commutative $R$-algebras with structure maps $\sigma,\sigma'$ is $R$-linear: it is additive, and $\varphi(r\cdot b)=\varphi(\sigma(r)b)=\varphi(\sigma(r))\varphi(b)=\sigma'(r)\varphi(b)=r\cdot\varphi(b)$. So the $A(u)$ and $\iota_i$ are $R$-linear, $i\mapsto A_i$ is a diagram of $R$-modules (functoriality is that of the algebra diagram), and $\iota_j\circ A(u)=\iota_i$ for $u:i\to j$ holds since $(A,(\iota_i))$ is a cocone of algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; hence $(A,(\iota_i))$ is a cocone of $R$-modules on this diagram.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778) and its proof: elements of a filtered colimit are classes of elements of the stages, sums and scalar multiples computed at a common later index; transcribed here to the colimit of commutative R-algebras regarded as R-modules

proof.text: *Step 3 (definition of $f$).* Let $P$ be an $R$-module and $f_i:A_i\to P$ $R$-linear with $f_j\circ A(u)=f_i$ for all $u:i\to j$. For $z\in A$ choose by step 1(b) $i$ and $a\in A_i$ with $z=\iota_i(a)$ and put $f(z)=f_i(a)$. This does not depend on the choice: if also $z=\iota_j(b)$ with $b\in A_j$, step 1(c) gives $k$, $u:i\to k$, $v:j\to k$ with $A(u)(a)=A(v)(b)$, so $f_i(a)=f_k(A(u)(a))=f_k(A(v)(b))=f_j(b)$. Taking the representation $z=\iota_i(a)$ itself gives $f(\iota_i(a))=f_i(a)$, i.e. $f\circ\iota_i=f_i$ for every $i$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778) and its proof: elements of a filtered colimit are classes of elements of the stages, sums and scalar multiples computed at a common later index; transcribed here to the colimit of commutative R-algebras regarded as R-modules

proof.text: *Step 4 ($f$ is $R$-linear).* Let $z,z'\in A$ and $r\in R$. By step 1(b) write $z=\iota_i(a)$, $z'=\iota_j(b)$. Since $I$ is filtered [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] there are an object $k$ and morphisms $u:i\to k$, $v:j\to k$; by the cocone identity of step 2, $z=\iota_k(a')$, $z'=\iota_k(b')$ with $a'=A(u)(a)$, $b'=A(v)(b)\in A_k$. As $\iota_k$ is $R$-linear (step 2), $z+z'=\iota_k(a'+b')$ and $r\cdot z=\iota_k(r\cdot a')$, so by step 3 and the $R$-linearity of $f_k$: $f(z+z')=f_k(a'+b')=f_k(a')+f_k(b')=f(z)+f(z')$ and $f(r\cdot z)=f_k(r\cdot a')=r\cdot f_k(a')=r\cdot f(z)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778) and its proof: elements of a filtered colimit are classes of elements of the stages, sums and scalar multiples computed at a common later index; transcribed here to the colimit of commutative R-algebras regarded as R-modules

proof.text: *Step 5 (uniqueness; conclusion).* If $g:A\to P$ is $R$-linear with $g\circ\iota_i=f_i$ for all $i$, then for $z\in A$, written $z=\iota_i(a)$ by step 1(b), $g(z)=f_i(a)=f(z)$; so $g=f$. With steps 2-4 this says that $(A,(\iota_i))$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto A_i$ in the category of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
